messages:
Anna (networking): follow-up from the ENI spike. key actionable: define handshake & failover semantics for ephemeral ENI agent.
Ben (infra): TL;DR: ENI path preserves src ip & is lower latency single-hop, but attach/warm latency and IAM surface worry me. central relay is simpler to onboard.
Mike (security): don't ship long-lived keys into customer accounts. handshake should use short-lived role assumption + signed ephemeral assertions (STS). KMS must be required for any customer-side signing.
Sara (product): compliance teams want explicit audit trail when traffic is switched to our relay. also customers expect cost transparency for data egress.
Anna (networking): proposed handshake outline: 1) customer creates role with limited trust + policy, 2) control plane pushes config blob (endpoint id, subnets), 3) agent assumes role, registers target with GWLBE, 4) agent opens health websocket to control plane and emits metrics.
Ben (infra): operational constraints: agent attach delay ~10-20s when cold, ENI limits per account matter. we need a warm pool strategy or warmup hints from control plane.
Mike (security): agent should rotate certs often. recommend ephemeral JWTs signed by control plane and validated by agent using public key cached in KMS. no private keys stored in control plane long-term.
Anna (networking): failover rules: if agent health webhook misses 2 intervals (30s interval) -> shift route to central relay and mark endpoint as degraded. TTL on DNS/route cache = 60s. manual cutover allowed.
Ben (infra): need a canary migration flow: start with low traffic customers, measure 95th p50 latency delta, error rates, and attach-failure incidence. automated rollback if error rate > 0.5% for 5m.
Sara (product): signal list for customers: source_ip_preserved (bool), egress_cost_estimate (USD/mo), audit_log_url, opt_in_required (bool). we'll use that in the UI.
Anna (networking): minimal agent API example:
```
POST /register {
  "endpoint_id": "ep-1234",
  "subnets": ["subnet-aaa","subnet-bbb"],
  "health_cb": "https://controlplane/api/health/ep-1234"
}
GET /health -> 200 {"status":"ok","uptime_s": 42}
```
Mike (security): sample trust policy sketch:
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::CONTROLPLANE_ACCOUNT:role/ep-agent"},
    "Action": "sts:AssumeRole",
    "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:RequestedRegion":"us-east-1"}}
  }]
}
```
Ben (infra): telemetry: agent must emit attach_time_ms, register_latency_ms, health_last_seen, bytes_in/out. control plane UI will surface 95/99 latency and attach failures.
Anna (networking): header propagation: preserve X-Forwarded-For where possible and add X-Redwood-Request-Id. if src ip not available (central relay), include original client ip in X-Original-Client header when available.
Sara (product): runbook note: customers get an onboarding checklist, with terraform snippet we provide, and an "uninstall" flow that flushes route registrations.
deploy-bot: created runbook: https://runbook.example.com/eni-optin-onboard (stub)
Ben (infra): migration mechanics: control plane will support 3 modes per endpoint: relay-only, eni-preferred, eni-strict. relay-only = default. eni-preferred = try ENI, failover allowed. eni-strict = reject if ENI not available.
Mike (security): require explicit customer opt-in for eni-strict. document key rotation cadence (every 24h) and compromise response.
Anna (networking): RFC TODOs: handshake API spec, terraform provider examples, UI flags & billing labels, metrics contract, operator runbook + rollback criteria. I'll draft and tag infra/security/product for review by EOD Friday.
Sara (product): thanks. i'll collate customer asks and create the UI mock.
Ben (infra): cool. also add an integration test that simulates ENI attach failures and validates failover under load.
Anna (networking): will do. ping me if you want to pair on the test harness. thanks everyone.
